extracted.intended_audience: social media marketers, brands, and TikTok content creators looking to optimize reach
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for creating and distributing TikTok content to maximize reach on the For You page by aligning with 2026 TikTok ranking factors and platform features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement (overall ranking factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the most important ranking factors for TikTok is engagement. This includes metrics like saves and shares, video likes, comments posted, videos completed, and favorited videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saves and shares often outweigh simple likes; finishing a long video or favoriting it signals strong resonance. TikTok may favor videos from creators whose content you regularly engage with. Optimize content to encourage these higher-weight engagement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saves and shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Save and share signals indicate high value and an intent to return or distribute content, often outweighing simple “Likes” by a significant margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create content that viewers want to revisit or send to others (how-tos, useful tips, strong calls-to-action to 'save for later' or share). Avoid content that looks ephemeral or purely promotional without utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video likes
rubrics_metrics.description: Likes are an engagement signal included under engagement metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likes matter but generally carry less weight than saves/shares and completion; use like prompts sparingly and focus on stronger engagement signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments posted
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are tracked as part of engagement and help signal interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage meaningful comments (questions, opinions) rather than low-effort emoji replies; reply to comments to boost interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Videos completed / completion rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether viewers finish a video is a key engagement signal; finishing a long video tells TikTok that content resonated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure videos to maximize retention (strong hook, narrative flow, value throughout). Monitor completion and audience retention in analytics and iterate to reduce drop-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favorited videos
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoriting a video is an explicit signal of user interest and intent to return to content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer content that warrants bookmarking (recipes, step-by-step guides, templates) to drive favorites.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interactions (accounts followed, content created, topic authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok considers user interactions such as accounts followed, content created, and topic authority to understand preferences and changes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build topic authority by consistently posting on a niche and encouraging users to follow. Creating original content in your niche helps the algorithm associate your account with that topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video information (captions, hashtags, sounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Video information like captions, hashtags and sounds helps TikTok understand and rank content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear captions, relevant hashtags and appropriate sounds to signal content topics. Include keywords in captions and overlays to aid algorithmic classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Value (spoken words / auto-captions / text overlays)
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithm analyzes spoken words via auto-captions and text overlays to match content to specific search queries, rewarding videos that provide direct answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design videos to answer common questions; speak key phrases aloud and include text overlays with target keywords. Treat TikTok as a search engine—optimize spoken and on-screen text for queries users might type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device and account indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok looks at device and account settings (country settings, language preferences, device type, category selection) to optimize performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indicators are used for optimization but generally hold less weight than engagement and user interactions. Be aware of locale and language targeting but prioritize strong relevance signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content exclusions (what the algorithm won’t show)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok states the platform aims to keep For You pages 'interesting', 'varied' and 'safe.' The algorithm does not recommend duplicate content, content you’ve already seen, content considered spam, potentially offensive or unsafe content, videos that have just been uploaded, or videos that are under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reposting identical content, spammy practices, and anything that could be flagged as unsafe. Understand that freshly uploaded or under-review content may not be surfaced until cleared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors the algorithm does not directly consider
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok mentions their algorithm does not directly consider follower count or previous high-performing videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New creators can still go viral; focus on signals of relevance and retention rather than raw follower numbers or relying on past hits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hashtag relevance and strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Hashtags help TikTok understand the content of a video and how to categorize it. Use hashtags that are relevant to your video and brand; leveraging trending hashtags can boost visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use relevant and trending hashtags (example: #cleaningmakeupbrushes, #satisfyingvideo). Browse the Hashtags tab to find top hashtags and post counts. Don’t use irrelevant hashtags merely to chase views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trends (audios, hashtags, effects, formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using trending audios, hashtags and effects can give videos a boost. Experimenting with trending video formats can help reach engaged audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put a unique spin on trends to stay true to brand voice. Monitor trending sounds, hashtags and formats and adopt those that align with your niche rather than jumping on every meme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook: make the first few seconds count
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok prioritizes whether users finished watching your video. You need to grab attention within the first few seconds—skip the intro and get straight to the good part within the first 2–3 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use immediate value propositions, text overlays, voiceovers or sound effects to hook viewers. Test hooks and analyze early drop-off to improve opening frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace longer short-form content (1 Minute+)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2026, the algorithm has shifted to reward videos over 1 minute long; videos between 60 and 90 seconds often see higher reach because they keep users on the app longer and allow for higher monetization RPM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If content allows, aim to cross the 1-minute threshold to unlock better distribution, but maintain punchiness and retention. Short clips still have a place—choose length based on content fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post at the right time (early engagement matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithm looks at engagements on your video to rank it; you need to drive as much engagement as possible within the first few minutes of posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post when your audience is most active (general best times: midweek afternoons/evenings 2–6 p.m., but check your audience analytics). Prompt early engagement through calls-to-action and distribution tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write keyword-rich captions (but don’t keyword-stuff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions should be relevant and include keywords to help the TikTok algorithm understand the content; avoid stuffing captions with keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, clear sentences that include strategic keywords relevant to the video. Example: Booking.com uses descriptive keywords like 'home,' 'view,' 'Cape Town.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Track performance using TikTok analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage TikTok analytics to get insights and refine strategy; key metrics include video views, play time and drop-off rates, traffic sources, likes/comments/shares, song uses, profile visits, follower growth, link clicks, video downloads and audience retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare different videos, lengths, captions and sounds to surface what resonates. Use data to iterate on hooks, formats and posting times. Consider Sprout Social or similar tools for cross-platform analytics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize content for search (TikTok SEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: With social media increasingly used as a search engine, craft descriptive, keyword-rich titles and captions that summarize visuals and highlight key themes. Spoken content and on-screen text overlays should reflect these keywords because the algorithm 'listens' to videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize for both native and web search (Google increasingly surfaces TikTok videos). Use clear descriptive language rather than cryptic captions; ensure captions, overlays and spoken words align on keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with TikTok influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborating with creators can introduce your brand to new communities; even nano or micro-influencers with a few thousand engaged followers can be valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider branded challenges, sponsored tutorials, unboxings, account takeovers and co-created products. Vet partners by analyzing audience quality, engagement rates, follower sentiment and brand alignment; set clear expectations and messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage Photo Mode and Swipe-Through Rate (STR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo Mode has its own algorithm based on Swipe-Through Rate (STR). If a user swipes through all photos, it signals high completion similar to watching a video to the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design carousels that encourage users to swipe to the last image. Treat STR like completion rate and optimize visuals/text to sustain interest across slides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate TikTok Shop strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok gives a visibility boost to content that integrates TikTok Shop features (like product anchors), provided the content is engaging and not purely spammy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If e-commerce is relevant, use Shop features thoughtfully—combine product anchors with high-value content and avoid overtly promotional or spammy posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified Views and the '200-view jail' phenomenon
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified Views are views longer than 5 seconds. The '200-view jail' happens when videos stop gaining reach after the initial test batch—often because the video failed to generate enough Qualified Views or had a low completion rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve early retention and Qualified Views by strengthening the hook and content value in the first 5 seconds; review and iterate if a video stalls near ~200 views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edutainment formula for virality
rubrics_metrics.description: The most consistent path to virality in 2026 is the 'edutainment formula': delivering value (education) in an entertaining format. Viral videos typically have a strong hook, offer high search value, and are under 90 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to educate while entertaining; structure videos to answer a question or solve a problem quickly and compellingly. Trigger share behavior by making content feel worth sending to a friend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting videos can negatively impact algorithmic signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Deleting videos removes data points the algorithm uses to understand your content, and mass-deleting can trigger spam filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to remove public visibility, set videos to 'Only Me' to preserve analytics and account history instead of deleting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-second rule (hook window) and Qualified Views distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The '3-second rule' refers to the critical window to grab attention before viewers scroll away. The algorithm also looks for 'Qualified Views' (5 seconds) in 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft hooks that secure attention within 2–3 seconds and keep viewers engaged past 5 seconds to count as Qualified Views. Use text overlays, immediate value, or surprising visuals early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting frequency and topic authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantity used to be primary, but in 2026 topic authority matters more. It is better to post 3–4 high-quality, search-optimized videos per week that fit your niche than to post low-effort daily content that confuses the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on consistent topical focus and quality rather than raw volume. Build authority by repeatedly covering the same themes and optimizing each post for search and retention.
